newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dividends to drive Belgian stocks higher.
newsitem.headline: Dividends to drive Belgian stocks higher.

text.p: The prospect of dividend payouts will support Belgian shares in the weeks ahead, with prices rising as long as bond yields remain at current low levels and the dollar holds up, dealers said on Monday.
"Now we are entering the coupon period. People don't want to sell, and others buy shares just for the coupons," one noted.

The Bel-20 index outpaced neighbouring French and Dutch markets to close 13.23 points or 0.61 percent higher at 2,196.43. Volume was a moderate 2.5 billion francs worth of Belgian shares, boosted by further buying of "baskets" of Bel-20 index stocks.
Among large gainers was Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL), which climbed 3.0 percent to 8,450 francs.
Analysts were puzzled as to the reason behind Monday's strong move, which some put down to the ongoing speculation that BBL would be part of a possible future Belgian bank merger.
"(But) the share is fully valued concerning the premium for a "big Belgian bank" prospect," one analyst said.

Among stocks to fall was Belgian shipping group CMB, hurt after details of 1996 results published at the weekend showed CMB's 1996 profit to be more disappointing than preliminary figures had shown. The stock fell 1.52 percent to 2,600 francs.
Generale Bank said in a research note it maintained the "sell" recommendation which it had given the stock back in January before the preliminary results were published.
CMB is also dollar sensitive and recovered from session lows as the dollar picked up during the day, dealers noted.

Other stocks with U.S. exposure include non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere, down 0.17 percent at 2,890 rancs, and oil major PetroFina, 0.2 percent lower at 12,750 francs. Retailer Delhaize, which gets most of its turnover from U.S. unit Food Lion, lagged the Bel-20 rise and climbed just 0.28 percent to 1,795 francs.
